analysis.title: 从模型竞速走向产品、算力与生态：本期 AI 趋势观察
analysis.lead: 本期共整理 129 条有效信号。下面不是新闻复述，而是把论文、公司、创业与政策放在同一张图里后的编辑性判断。
paragraphs: 研究侧共收录 20 条信号，重点包括 《BACE: LLM-based Code Generation through Bayesian Anchored…》、《Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents…》。与只看榜单相比，更值得持续观察的是论文能否把 Agent 的可靠性、评测完整性与推理成本一起向前推进。
AI 跨领域贡献收录 16 条，代表性事件包括 《Claude Fable 5 协助找到雅可比猜想的显式三维反例》、《OpenAI 模型推翻平面单位距离问题中的长期猜想》。这类结果会区分官方论文、可核验反例、媒体报道与尚待同行评审的社交平台首发，避免把‘可计算验证’和‘完成学术确认’混为一谈。
中国 AI 板块本期收录 16 条动态，已覆盖 DeepSeek。代表性变化包括 《邦彦云PC推出 DeepSeek 智能问答AI助手本地化部署方案》、《DeepSeek 发布 补偿通知》；竞争正在从单次模型发布延伸到开源策略、Agent 产品入口、国产算力适配和价格体系。
产业侧共有 28 条前沿实验室与大厂动态、14 条关键人物公开信号，另有 13 条创业和 10 条政策安全更新。模型能力、算力供给、创始人判断、产品分发与合规成本正在变成同一个竞争问题。

items.summary: We present tinyGist, an efficient decentralized federated learning framework designed for tiny microcontrollers. items.title: WiP: Quantum-Assisted Secure ISAC with Encrypted Inference
items.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) reuses a wireless waveform for data delivery and environmental perception, but this coupling exposes communication payloads, sensing semantics, and downstream inference to a common attacker. items.title: Going Faster: Privacy-Preserving Shortest Paths from Start to End
items.summary: Finding shortest paths in graphs is a fundamental combinatorial optimization problem with numerous applications, e. g., in graph centrality measures, computational biology, and business process analysis. To address privacy constraints in such applications, Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) protocols can compute the lengths of shortest paths on secret-shared graphs. Many such protocols have been proposed in the past, but they only compute the lengths of the shortest paths and not the paths themselves.

items.title: Verifiable Blind Pseudonymization via Polymorphic Encryption Using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
items.summary: Pseudonymization is a basic technique for privacy protection, limiting identifiability and linkability of data. Data can be pseudonymized blindly, i.e., while being end-to-end encrypted, using the Polymorphic Encryption and Pseudonymization (PEP) framework. This means that the party performing pseudonymization does not see the values of pseudonyms and cannot determine if two (encrypted) pseudonyms belong to each other, ensuring confidentiality and unlinkability. The pseudonymizing party can, however, unnoticeably corrupt any data being exchanged. This violates integrity.
